questions.prompt: A switch has a configured usable PoE budget of 240 W and 220 W is already reserved. A replacement AP requires a 30 W reservation; its old AP reserved 10 W. Per-port limits permit either. What happens if the old AP is removed before installing the replacement?

choices.text: The replacement still exceeds budget by 30 W
choices.explanation: Removing the old reservation frees another 10 W.

choices.text: The new reservation fits exactly at 240 W total
The budget becomes 270 W because reservations compound forever
choices.explanation: A released reservation does not remain charged indefinitely in this scenario.

choices.text: The switch supplies only 20 W regardless of the request
choices.explanation: The stated new request fits after releasing the old 10 W.

questions.explanation: Account for the removed device as well as the new allocation. The net increase is 20 W, equal to the original spare budget.

choices.explanation: UDP provides no deadline guarantee.

choices.text: UDP eliminates all application sequencing needs

questions.prompt: The specified EUI-64 process converts MAC A4-B1-C1-02-03-04 into an interface identifier. Which TWO steps are correct? Select two.

choices.text: Change first byte A4 to A6
choices.explanation: XOR A4 with 02 to invert the U/L bit.

choices.text: Change first byte A4 to A5
choices.explanation: That changes the low-order multicast bit instead.

choices.text: Append FF-FE after all six MAC bytes
choices.explanation: The inserted pair belongs in the middle.

choices.text: Reverse the order of 02-03-04
choices.explanation: The MAC byte order is retained.

choices.text: Insert FF-FE between C1 and 02
